newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended mostly lower but off lows on arbitrage selling against New York. January added $1 to close at $1,331 per tonne, while March lost $2 to close at $1,262 per tonne. May ended at $1,217 per tonne, a decline of $8 per tonne. There were no market-moving news.

In New York the expiring December contract pushed higher for the third day this week causing the spread to widen further. Unlike the previous two sessions, however, March and the deferred positions were not able to follow the lead of the spot contract and instead eased slightly.

While supplies might remain quite limited for the spot contract, the situation may change in the not so distant future. On Friday the USDA is expected to release its 1996/97 coffee balance estimates. This will be followed by US Green Coffee Association coffee stock data on Monday, along with London certified coffee stock figures for November.

No changes are expected in the USDA figures but traders said they cannot rule out any surprises. The USDA could revise its 1996/97 crop estimate for Brazil of 27.5 million 60-kg bags and make a preliminary forecast for Brazil's 1997/98 season, traders said.
December added 1.25 cents/lb to close at 119.00 cents/lb while March gave up 10 points to close at 108.10 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 30 and 40 points.

COLOMBIA - After talks in Bogota with Ivorian Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze and Abel Rwendire of Uganda Jorge Cardenas, head of Colombia's National Coffee Growers Federation, said that they all agreed that there is a need to increase the amount of coffee withheld under the ACPC retention plan during the first half of 1997 by about 2.5 million 60-kg bags.

Gauze called last month, during the Inter- African coffee organization's general assembly in Abidjan, for an emergency ACPC meeting to discuss tightening the 1996/97 ACPC export limit programme and agree on a response to increased exports by non-members such as Mexico, Guatemala and Vietnam.
BRAZIL - The Brazilian government will auction 90,018 60- kg bags of coffee stocks in its next monthly auction on December 9, official sources said.

The auction will be the largest so far in a series of monthly sales planned for this coffee year (July/June). In November, the government sold 63,084 60-kg bags of coffee or 37.81 per cent of its auction of 85,466 bags of stocks.

ETHIOPIA - According to official sources coffee exports in 1996/97 (October/September) are likely to reach 1.8 million 60-kg bags - the highest export volume in the country's trade history. It was added that the country exported 1.7 million bags in 1995/96 which earned it $279.5 million - lower than the $300.9 million it received for exporting 1.3 million 60-kg bags of coffee in 1994/95.
These figures, however, include only legal exports and the country's production figures suggest that actual exports were significantly higher.

BRAZIL - Santos exporter Icatu/Sumatra said that Brazil's coffee production in 1997/98 may drop to 24 million 60-kg bags after 27.65 million bags in 1996/97. The highest estimate for 1997/98 is above 32 million bags and more precise estimates could be delayed until February because some coffee-growing regions had up to five flowerings, a factor which could also reduce the overall quality expectation.

FINLAND - Finland imported 72,598 bags of coffee in August 1996 nearly 37 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 784,100 bags, 56 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 fell sharply by 44 per cent to 758,500 bags.
The main suppliers of green coffee in January/August 1996 were Costa Rica (100,000 vs 76,800 bags), Guatemala (139,900 vs 66,000 bags) and Colombia (176,000 vs 134,100 bags).
